look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check the BASE of a mature clump for short, hard, KNOTTY RHIZOMES, then inspect the narrow cylindrical bristly seedhead. Several bristles subtend each 2–3 mm spikelet; a magnifier helps. The rhizomatous perennial base is the practical tie-breaker against annual yellow foxtail (Setaria pumila), which has fibrous roots. Do not identify this species from bristle color alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Setaria pumila has a similar yellowish, densely bristly head but is typically an annual with fibrous roots and NO knotty rhizomes. Setaria viridis typically has fewer bristles per spikelet. Examine rootstock and mature spikelets, not color or head shape alone.
diagnostic_sequence: Inspect the basal rootstock for short hard knotty rhizomes; do not uproot protected or sensitive plants.
Use a hand lens on spikelets: several bristles at each base; spikelets approximately 2–3 mm.
Photograph leaf ligule and a complete plant habit; existing single macro does not show the decisive rhizome.
